pr_title: Fail shard if STARTED after master failover
pr_body:
If `cluster.no_master_block: all` then we remove all shards locally
whenever there's no master, but there might still be a shard-started
message in flight. When the new master is elected we start to recover
our shards again and the stale shard-started message could arrive and
move this shard to `STARTED` in the cluster state too soon. This is
pretty rare so we fix it by just failing the shard and starting the
recovery again.

Closes #87367

Looks like this started failing every few days starting around 25 Feb.
Failed on my CI machine after ~1000 iterations with `stress-ng --timeout 0 --cpu 16` running in the background.

When `cluster.no_master_block: all` we close every shard when the master node goes `null` in order to recover them from scratch again. However if there's a shard-started message in flight then `ShardStateAction` will retry it on the new master, and that can arrive after the shard started initialising again.

Basically I think this assertion is bogus. If we see its condition as `false` we should just fail the shard and restart its recovery.
... however, I'm unable to explain exactly why this started happening around 25 Feb. I think it could have happened before too. Maybe it was just some performance improvements that affected timing?

review_comments: I think this can only happen when the shard is a replica, since if it was or is now a primary, we would be in a new primary term, which would make the shard started message be skipped by the master. Can we assert that?

Yes it looks like this can only affect replicas. I added a comment and assertion to that effect in [08cd9bb](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/87451/commits/08cd9bbb790b4ba50d67ab92cf1a795c6c0c0245).
